lessons.title: Entities, attributes and records
lessons.prepare: Open the entities and relationships chapter, relationships-workbook.md, relationships-answers.md, equipment-model.svg and the four model CSVs (Borrower, Category, Equipment, Loan). Use fictional data and a disposable copy or paper. No SQL setup or student account is required. Explained answers are public.

slides.title: Entities, attributes and records
body: Unit 2 · Week 2 · Lesson 1
Explain what each table, row and field represents.
slides.notes: Use the equipment desk scenario from Week 1. Explain what each table, row and field represents. All activities are ungraded. Suggested timings can be adjusted. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: The facts that need a home
body: Why did repeating a borrower’s label cause a problem?
What does one row in the Loan table represent?
slides.notes: A label change could leave inconsistent labels for the same borrower in the flat register. A Loan row represents one borrowing event. Recall the separate homes for borrower, item and loan facts before introducing Category. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: Type, instance and attribute
table: Loan: the kind of event we record
DueDate: a property of a loan
slides.notes: An entity is one distinguishable thing or event. An entity type groups similar entities. An attribute is a property. In this relational model, a table represents the entity type, a record represents an instance, and a column or field represents an attribute. The value 2026-04-06 is not the field definition itself. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: A row and its fields
body: Loan L001 records one event for borrower B001 and item E01.
DueDate names a field. 2026-04-06 is L001’s value in it.
Another loan has its own row and its own values.
slides.notes: Show L001 in model-loans.csv and compare it with L002. Ask learners to point to an entire record, a column heading and one field value. Keep DueDate as a date property of an event, rather than a permanent property of an equipment item. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: The new Category table
table: One item category, such as Audio
slides.notes: Category extends Week 1’s three-table sketch. Category assignments are a new design decision: Camera is Imaging, Tripod is Support, Recorder and Microphone are Audio. Model categories has three records, borrowers four, equipment five and loans six. A category may exist before any equipment refers to it. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: Annotated table definitions
body: Open the four model CSVs. Label a table, row and field.
Choose one attribute and give a stored value for it.
Explain why an equipment description cannot identify every item.
slides.notes: Use workbook questions 1–2. E01 and E04 both have description Camera, so that description is not unique. EquipmentID distinguishes each physical item under the agreed rules. Ask for labelled examples rather than definitions copied without context. No SQL creation is needed. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: The column and the value
body: A classmate says “2026-04-06 is an attribute name.”
Explain the difference between DueDate and that date.
slides.notes: DueDate is the attribute or column name. 2026-04-06 is the value of that attribute for L001. A record includes the values for one instance across its defined fields. Ask students to use a different Loan row as their fresh example. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: A fresh record
body: A new item E06 also has the description Camera.
Explain why it needs its own record and identifier.
slides.notes: E06 represents another physical item even if its description matches E01 and E04. It requires a unique EquipmentID and a valid required CategoryID. No new loan is implied simply by registering an item. A sample’s unique-looking description does not establish a permanent uniqueness rule. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

lessons.title: Primary, foreign and composite keys
lessons.prepare: Open the entities and relationships chapter, relationships-workbook.md, relationships-answers.md, equipment-model.svg and the four model CSVs (Borrower, Category, Equipment, Loan). Use fictional data and a disposable copy or paper. No SQL setup or student account is required. Explained answers are public.

slides.title: Primary, foreign and composite keys
body: Unit 2 · Week 2 · Lesson 2
Choose keys that preserve valid borrowing history.
slides.notes: Use the equipment desk scenario from Week 1. Choose keys that preserve valid borrowing history. All activities are ungraded. Suggested timings can be adjusted. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: Matching descriptions
body: E01 and E04 are both Camera.
Which field distinguishes the items? What rule must it follow?
slides.notes: EquipmentID identifies each item. The chosen primary key must be unique and required. Descriptions and borrower display labels can repeat. A primary key may use one field or a group of fields. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: Keys and their jobs
table: A minimal set that uniquely identifies a row
The candidate key chosen for identification
A reference to a permitted key
A key containing more than one attribute
slides.notes: Minimal means no attribute can be removed without losing uniqueness under the agreed rules. Minimal does not mean shortest text. A composite key can be a primary key. A foreign key may refer to another table or the same table and its values may repeat. Our required foreign keys refer to existing parent primary keys. Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html . Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: A loan uses three identifiers
slides.notes: Trace L003 to Borrower B001 (Learner A), Equipment E03 (Recorder), then Equipment.CategoryID C03 to Category C03 (Audio). Equipment.CategoryID is another required FK. The foreign keys identify the referenced borrower and item, not this loan event. BorrowerID repeats in Loan because borrowers can have multiple events. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: A pair that can repeat
body: B002 borrowed E02 in L005 and again in L002.
The pair (BorrowerID, EquipmentID) repeats legitimately.
LoanID distinguishes these two borrowing events.
slides.notes: These are the two existing events in the dataset. L005 is returned, L002 is active. Do not use the borrower/item pair alone as Loan’s key. Adding a new future event needs a new LoanID and separate checks against overlapping active loans. An FK alone does not enforce that business rule. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: Keys that reject the right errors
body: Find every PK and FK in the four model tables.
Explain duplicate LoanID L001 and borrower reference B999.
Workshop rule: one enrolment per borrower/workshop pair.
Which fields together could identify an enrolment?
slides.notes: Use workbook questions 2, 3, 6, 7 and 9 as selected practice. Duplicate L001 violates PK uniqueness. B999 is absent from Borrower, so a required FK must reject it. For the separate WorkshopEnrolment example, assume one enrolment per borrower/workshop pair: (BorrowerID, WorkshopID) can be a composite PK. Either field alone may repeat. Example pairs B001/W01, B001/W02 and B002/W01 are permitted, while another B001/W01 is not. The extension is not a fifth table in the equipment model. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: A repeated foreign key
body: B001 appears in the BorrowerID field of two Loan rows.
Does this break key uniqueness? Explain which key matters.
slides.notes: No. BorrowerID is a foreign key in Loan and may repeat. LoanID is the chosen primary key of Loan and must remain unique. B001 must exist in Borrower for both references. A field can have different key roles in different tables. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: Rules beyond the sample
body: A small dataset has no repeated borrower labels.
Explain why this alone does not make the label a candidate key.
slides.notes: Candidate-key status depends on the intended rules for all valid data, including future records. The school may register two borrowers with the same label. A sample can expose a failed uniqueness claim but cannot establish a permanent uniqueness requirement by itself. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: Reading and drawing relationships
body: Unit 2 · Week 2 · Lesson 3
Read relationship limits in both directions.
slides.notes: Use the equipment desk scenario from Week 1. Read relationship limits in both directions. All activities are ungraded. Suggested timings can be adjusted. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: One borrower, several events
body: Borrower B001 appears in loans L001 and L003.
Does each loan still refer to exactly one borrower?
slides.notes: Yes. The two directions have different counts. One borrower can have many Loan rows. Each Loan row has one required borrower reference. Ask students to state the direction before naming the relationship. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: Minimum and maximum participation
slides.notes: Zero means optional participation. Exactly one means minimum one and maximum one. The Equipment–Loan rule follows the same pattern: an item can have zero or many loans over time, and each loan has exactly one item. Read the symbols at one end as the number there for one instance at the other end. Rules come from requirements, not only the observed sample. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: The four-table equipment model
slides.notes: Two bars mark exactly one. A circle and a crow’s foot mark zero or many. Read Category–Equipment, Borrower–Loan and Equipment–Loan in both directions. Each parent permits zero or many children; each child requires exactly one parent. PK means primary key and FK means foreign key. Primary keys are underlined. Original diagram source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/equipment-model.svg . Notation reference: SCSA support booklet, printed page 15 (PDF page 19). The diagram’s placements can change without changing its meaning. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

diagram.alt: Four-table equipment ER model. Category to Equipment, Equipment to Loan, and Borrower to Loan each allow zero or many children. Every child requires exactly one parent. PKs are underlined and FKs labelled.

slides.title: Three relationship patterns
table: Each borrower has at most one locker, and vice versa
One item can have many loan events over time
Borrowers can use many items, and vice versa
slides.notes: The locker example states maximum participation only. Whether a borrower must have a locker is a separate minimum-participation rule. Borrowing across time is many to many between Borrower and Equipment; Loan resolves it into two one-to-many relationships and stores event facts. This does not permit two active loans for the same physical item simultaneously. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: An independent four-table diagram
body: Redraw the model with PKs underlined and FKs labelled.
State each connection in both directions.
Check the zero-or-many and exactly-one ends.
slides.notes: Use workbook questions 4, 5 and 8. Hide the worked model while learners draw, then compare. Category–Equipment, Equipment–Loan and Borrower–Loan all have optional-many at the child end and exactly-one at the parent end. Preserve all four tables and their fields. Ask partners to explain how the required FK is on the many side. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: A category with no items
body: New category C04 has no equipment yet.
Does this break the model? What about an item with no category?
slides.notes: C04 is allowed because a category may have zero items. An Equipment row with no CategoryID breaks the required category rule. Students should point to the appropriate end of the relationship instead of assuming all participation is mandatory. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: History and current availability
body: One item has several Loan rows across its history.
Explain why this does not mean it can be on two active loans.
slides.notes: History records events over time. The minimum/maximum relationship does not by itself enforce the separate no-overlap rule for active loans. The application or database needs an appropriate additional check. Ask for one unreturned and one returned example rather than assuming every Loan row is current. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: Data dictionaries and model checks
body: Unit 2 · Week 2 · Lesson 4
Document each field and test the design against examples.
slides.notes: Use the equipment desk scenario from Week 1. Document each field and test the design against examples. All activities are ungraded. Suggested timings can be adjusted. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: A diagram and a dictionary
body: The diagram shows tables and their connections.
What else must a developer know before creating the fields?
A data dictionary defines each field’s type, size and rules.
slides.notes: A data dictionary records field names, types, sizes, meanings and constraints. It complements the diagram. Include required/optional status, key roles, formats and defaults where relevant. The model uses conceptual types before mapping to a chosen DBMS. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: Loan identifiers in the dictionary
slides.notes: The dictionary gives maximum text lengths chosen for this exercise, not universal limits. BorrowerID follows B plus three digits and EquipmentID E plus two digits. Text preserves letters and leading zeros. Each FK refers to the matching identifier field in its parent table. The exact DBMS type and enforcement come later. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: Dates, return status and defaults
table: Required; default False for a new loan
slides.notes: Date and Boolean storage sizes depend on the DBMS. A displayed date format is not necessarily the storage format. The False default applies when a new loan omits a status value; it does not reset historical loans. CSV values are text encodings until converted. Choose integer for counts, float for approximate measured mass, text for labels, date for due date and Boolean for return status. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: Counterexamples for a design
table: New category C04 with no items
slides.notes: Partners state allowed/refused and explain the specific rule. Duplicate L001 and nonexistent B999 are invalid. For this learning model, restrict deletion of B001 while loans refer to it until references are resolved deliberately. C04 with no equipment is allowed. Format checks alone cannot prove a stored fact is true. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: Dictionary and workbook practice
body: Write all five Loan field definitions, including constraints.
Complete the relevant workbook questions independently.
Compare the explained answers, then correct one weak rule.
slides.notes: Use workbook questions 10–12 and revisit question 7. Loan has LoanID, BorrowerID, EquipmentID, DueDate and Returned. Include type, maximum text size or DBMS-dependent size, meaning, key/reference, required status and relevant format/default. Identifiers are text. Default False applies to new loans. Ask for a justified deletion policy that keeps loan history. Support learners with the worked tables before a fresh independent example. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: A default is not a bulk update
body: A returned historical loan has Returned=True.
The design specifies default False for new loans.
Does the default change that old loan? Explain.
slides.notes: No. A default supplies a value for a new record when omitted in the appropriate operation. It does not rewrite existing records. Changing an existing record needs an explicit update, which must also meet the configured constraints. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

slides.title: A new requirement changes the model
body: New rule: one loan event may contain several equipment items.
Can one EquipmentID field represent every item in that event?
slides.notes: A single EquipmentID stores one item reference. Do not overwrite the field or store a comma-separated list while claiming the existing design is unchanged. Further modelling could separate the loan event from its item lines in a linking/detail table, with agreed item and return rules. Ask which facts belong to the whole event and which belong to each item. This is an extension discussion, not a silent change to the four-table dataset. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.
